legacy_cells.B: Machine Learning-Augmented Triage for Sepsis: Real-Time ICU Mortality Prediction Using SHAP-Explained Meta-Ensemble Models
legacy_cells.C: Hülya Yilmaz Başer; Turan Evran; Mehmet Akif Cifci
legacy_cells.I: 005_2025_Machine Learning-Augmented Triage for Sepsis Real-Time ICU Mortality Prediction Using SHAP-Explained Meta-Ensemble Models.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Sepsis, with in-hospital mortality as the prediction target
legacy_cells.S: Among adult sepsis patients admitted from the ED to the ICU, who will die during the hospitalization?
legacy_cells.T: Adults (≥18 years) admitted directly from the ED to ICU with suspected sepsis. The article reports a final cohort of 1,000 patients.
legacy_cells.V: Support sepsis triage, including prioritizing ICU transfer or reassessment
legacy_cells.AI: Structured EMR/EHR data; demographics, vital signs, laboratory markers, clinical scores, derived biomarkers
legacy_cells.AN: Continuous variables were mean-imputed and categorical variables mode-imputed. SMOTE was applied to training folds for class imbalance.
legacy_cells.CR: Brier score calibration was evaluated: 0.118 internally and 0.124 on external MIMIC-III validation.
legacy_cells.DN: Tertiary academic hospital EMR and MIMIC-III
legacy_cells.DQ: Internal cohort: 1,000 patients. MIMIC-III source is described as over 40,000 ICU admissions. External test-subset size is not reported.
legacy_cells.DR: Two data sources/cohorts are described: a tertiary hospital and MIMIC-III. The paper does not clearly identify the primary hospital consistently.
legacy_cells.EI: Non-WM comparisons in the internal cohort: qSOFA AUROC 0.78, NEWS 0.81, Random Forest 0.92, Gradient Boosting 0.93, Logistic Regression 0.89, and Stacked Ensemble 0.96.
legacy_cells.EL: The internal validation confusion matrix reports 56 false negatives and 42 false positives.
legacy_cells.EO: The authors state that hospital EMR data were extracted, anonymized, and stored securely.
legacy_cells.EP: The dashboard presents SHAP explanations alongside mortality-risk probabilities and decision suggestions, while physicians retain decision authority.
legacy_cells.EQ: The paper states adherence to the Declaration of Helsinki and alignment with Turkey’s Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 and GDPR Article 89(1). FDA AI/ML guidelines are mentioned as an expectation, not demonstrated compliance.
legacy_cells.ER: Pamukkale University Non-Interventional Clinical Research Ethics Committee. Methods report Approval No. 2024-521152. The declarations give protocol E-60116787-020-521152, dated 2 May 2024.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors propose a stacked mortality-prediction ensemble using Random Forest and Gradient Boosting base learners with Logistic Regression aggregation, tuned with Red Piranha Optimization and explained with SHAP.
legacy_cells.FN: Internal results: AUROC 0.96, accuracy 0.90, precision 0.85, recall 0.81, F1-score 0.83, and Brier score 0.118. External MIMIC-III AUROC was 0.94 ± 0.01 with Brier score 0.124.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors identify the single-center retrospective dataset as a limitation, say prospective multi-institutional studies are needed, and state that the current model uses static features. They also call for fairness auditing and clinician-in-the-loop evaluation.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors suggest extending the ensemble with temporal encoders such as transformers or LSTMs for dynamic risk stratification and conducting prospective multi-institutional studies.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors frame the gap as the inability of conventional fixed-threshold scores to capture individualized risk and nonlinear relationships in sepsis data.
legacy_cells.FR: The reported system predicts an in-hospital mortality label from static clinical features. No persistent patient state, learned temporal transition, action-conditioned rollout, counterfactual identification, or planning result is demonstrated. The dashboard and prospective benefit remain claims or proposed use, not evaluated clinical outcomes.
legacy_cells.FT: Reusable lesson: keep static risk classification distinct from a world model. The authors themselves identify temporal encoders as a needed extension before claiming dynamic risk stratification.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF text, pp. 1–27: title and abstract (p. 1), Introduction and Literature Review (pp. 2–6), Methods including cohort, preprocessing, architecture, model evaluation and external validation (pp. 6–18), Results and Tables 1–5 plus error analysis (pp. 6–21), Discussion, limitations and Conclusions (pp. 22–24), ethics and data availability statements (p. 24), references and disclaimer (pp. 25–27). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The article is clearly a static mortality classifier rather than a world model. Internal cohort descriptions conflict: the final cohort is 1,000 patients, another passage says 3,000 were reduced to 1,000, and the RPO section describes 45,000 encounters. The external MIMIC-III source is described as over 40,000 admissions, but the test subset size is unstated. The paper also varies in cohort criteria and reports differing ethics approval identifiers. Text extraction shows some irregular table/formula layout, so no ambiguous table cells were used. A:I were left unchanged. Evidence QA: 44/51 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (86.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Schema normalization (source details retained): DO normalized to 'Multiple'; source detail: Clinical EMR records and the MIMIC-III database Codex audit: 50 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 1 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All 27 PDF pages, references 1–58, equations and Algorithm 1 read. All pages rendered; figures 1–8 and Tables 1–5 visually inspected on pp. 2,4,6,9,12,13,15,16,17,19,20,21,22. No included appendix/supplement.

Source inconsistencies in cohorts, target, preprocessing and metrics remain unresolved; R2/R3 identify reported study designs, not independently reproduced reliability. No R4–R8, prospective patient benefit, causal validity or calibrated-trajectory claim is assigned.
External dataset selection size is unreported; database-wide >40,000 admissions must not become this study external sample size.
Article data-release DOI and code/weights were not retrieved. Claimed dashboard is not evidence of real deployment or human study.
Single-model extraction with skeptical reread and visual checks, no independent human review.
notes: Legacy Exclude / static prediction is retained. BP_COMPONENT marks possible component-level study, not a newly included world model. Table versus figure AUROC values are retained as separate scoped results; none is averaged away. SHAP explains model association, not patient-specific causal effects.
